title: This Photo Almost Didn’t Make the Cut – Nicholas Haig-Arack
content:
A behind-the-scenes photograph of the editorial staff at The Radavist, captured during a staff dinner during the 2026 Made Bike Show weekend, makes our Copy Editor reflect on what makes this site special…


At first I thought this picture wasn’t good enough to publish on The Radavist. After all, we’ve set a pretty high bar for ourselves when it comes to the photographic content on this site.

But this group photo grew on me.

It’s not just because it’s a rare picture of our team in one place. It captures something real, something fallible, about this rag-tag bunch of messy little humans who make up the editorial team of The Radavist.

One of the things I love most about The Radavist is that it’s made by real people. In an era of instant gratification, artificial intelligence, and convenience that comes at the cost of all else, it feels countercultural to offer a compassionate, personality-driven take on the world of bicycles. That’s precisely what we’ve envisioned for The Radavist as a whole – it’s not just one person; it’s a family. We all come from different places and offer different points of view, but ultimately we are all connected by the transformative powers of riding bikes.

Our group photo was shot on my Fuji X30 digital camera by Gwen, my domestic partner, outside of Akadi, a West African restaurant in Portland, after our annual staff get-together at Made. From left to right, there’s me, Mara, John, Paul, Cari, and Spencer. Missing from the photo: Travis, Miguel, Hailey, and Joshua. Hopefully someday we can get the whole team together in one place! That’s one of the beautiful things about Made and other events like it – it gives us a reason to gather.

It was really a pleasure to meet so many of you at Made, and we’re looking forward to more in-person events to strengthen these real-world connections. Thanks for being a part of it.
